title: Machine Learning Engineer, Multimodal Perception and Authentication
description:
About the Team

The Future of Computing Research team is an applied research team within OpenAI’s Consumer Devices group. We study how AI systems perceive people and their surroundings, and we turn that research into capabilities for future products.

 

Our work spans machine learning, sensing, and hardware, with a focus on building systems that work beyond controlled environments.

 

About the Role

We’re looking for a machine learning engineer to help shape how future AI systems understand the physical world and the people in it. The role focuses on multimodal perception and authentication, bringing together signals from cameras, microphones, and other sensors.

 

You’ll work with specialized perception models and larger multimodal models, and partner with hardware, firmware, software, and product teams to bring new research into real-world systems.

 

This role is based in San Francisco. We work in the office three days per week and offer relocation assistance.

 

In this role, you will:

- Research and develop multimodal perception and authentication methods across visual, audio, and other sensing signals.

- Explore how specialized perception models and larger multimodal models can work together.

- Design data, training, and evaluation approaches that improve performance in real-world conditions.

- Study model behavior, robustness, and failure modes across sensing, data, and deployment environments.

- Integrate and validate new capabilities in real-time or resource-constrained systems.

- Work with hardware, firmware, software, and product teams to turn research into working systems.

 

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have a strong background in computer vision, audio or speech machine learning, multimodal learning, or sensing.

- Have experience developing specialized machine learning models, larger multimodal models, or both.

- Have brought research ideas into practical systems, prototypes, or products.

- Know how to design experiments, build evaluations, and investigate model behavior.

- Have worked with sensing hardware, real-time systems, or other deployment constraints.

- Are proficient in Python and PyTorch and comfortable with C++ or systems integration.

- Have experience with authentication, biometrics, or other privacy-sensitive applications.

- Enjoy working across disciplines on research problems that are still taking shape.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. title: Staff / Principal Product Designer, Design Systems
description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for startups. Open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books - all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Rho - New York (in person)

Rho is building the best business banking platform on earth. Not "one of." The best. We are not being cute about that.

We're looking for a Staff or Principal Product Designer to own our design system, the governed, in code foundation that everything we ship stands on. This is not a role where you maintain a Figma library and file tickets. This is the role where you define the frontend layer of a financial operating system that companies trust with their money.

It's a long post on purpose. We'd rather you know exactly what this is before you apply.

What you'd actually own

Our design system is becoming the governed frontend layer of the product, components in code, rules enforced through lint and CI, documentation an AI agent can query and build against on spec. You would own that. The architecture, the tokens, the primitives, the motion language, the governance, the contribution model, and the standards that let 80 plus engineers and PMs ship on bar without a designer babysitting every pixel.

You'll partner with our frontend guild, our engineers, and the design team as genuine equals, not as a service desk. You'll decide what a component is, how it behaves, how it moves, what it enables, and where it must not bend. You'll set the craft bar for the entire org and then build the system that makes hitting that bar the path of least resistance.

Who this is for

You've been doing this for a while. We mean it, at least 7 years of product design experience, with real design systems ownership at scale. Not "contributed to a design system." Owned one. Built one. Governed one. Watched it get abused and fixed the governance so it couldn't happen again.

You are the kind of person who:

- Designs in code, or is hungry to. You believe Figma is not the build environment, and that designing in the real medium eliminates a whole category of hidden QA cost. If the phrase "design engineer" makes you lean forward, hi.

- Has genuine taste and a serious bar for it. Branding, typography, motion, microinteractions: you sweat all of it. You have opinions about easing curves and you can defend them. A transition that feels half a beat off bothers you until it's fixed.

- Owns your craft, doesn't inherit it. You can point at a visual language and say "I built that," not "that was set before I got there and I adjusted the fonts."

- Builds systems, not screens. You think in primitives, states, edge cases, and two-way doors. When something breaks at a thousand users, you already designed for it.

- Ships, then sharpens. You move fast, you work out loud, you share the messy middle instead of disappearing for three weeks and returning with a monument. Perfect but late is a fail here.

- Has low ego and high standards at the same time. You hold a firm craft bar and you genuinely want the critique. You defend decisions with reasoning, not with "it's my stylistic choice."

- Gets the domain, or is dying to. Financial workflows are dense, multi-role, permission scoped, and unforgiving. You find that fun, not frightening.

Who this is NOT for

A few honest filters, to save us both time.

Do not apply to this role if you are junior. This is a Staff/Principal position. If you're earlier in your career, we'd genuinely love to meet you, we just want you in the right process. Apply for our product designer role instead: https://www.rho.co/careers/f4ece49b-3b53-4ffb-861f-9cc972c10b27

It's also probably not your fit if:

- Your portfolio is process decks, tiny mockups, and journey maps, and the actual UI is nowhere to be found. We evaluate craft at the pixel level. If we can't see it, we can't hire it.

- Your idea of a design system is a color palette and a component library nobody governs.

- Motion and micro interaction
